statement.p: Compute the derivative of the given function in two different ways.
a) Use the Product Rule, [fg]' = f\cdot g' + f' \cdot g. (Fill in each blank, then simplify.)
b) Use algebra first to simplify h, then differentiate without the Product Rule.

static.solution:
Solution:
First, using the Product Rule,
\begin{array}{rcl} h'(s) \amp =\amp (-7 s - 3) \cdot \frac{d}{dx}[ -7 s + 1 ] + \frac{d}{dx}[ -7 s - 3 ] (-7 s + 1)\\ \amp \amp \\ \amp =\amp (-7 s - 3)(-7) + (-7)(-7 s + 1) \\ \end{array} After simplifying the last line, we find h'(s) = 98 s + 14.
Next, simplify h first. Then take the derivative. \begin{array}{rcl} h(s) \amp =\amp (-7 s - 3)(-7 s + 1) = 49 s^2 + 14 s - 3 \\ \amp \amp \\ h'(s) \amp =\amp 98 s + 14 \end{array} The two simplified answers should match.
